body:
Gold markets are pricing in the sharp August rally that has pushed spot toward the mid-$4,300s to $4,400s. Gold rose to 4,429.49 USD/t.oz on August 18, 2026, up 0.30% from the previous day, and over the past month gold's price has risen 10.52%, and is up 33.53% compared to the same time last year. The move has been attributed largely to shifting Fed rate expectations: gold opened at its highest level since early June following a disappointing employment report that prompted many analysts to pare back their expectations of a rate increase by the Fed. This macro backdrop shows up cleanly in the order books: both Kalshi's above $4,331.99 and above $4,371.99 August-settlement contracts and Polymarket's Aug 18/19 up-or-down contracts are pricing near even money, exactly where you'd expect strikes to cluster around a spot price bouncing through the low $4,400s.

The scanner flagged exactly one cross-platform opportunity today, and it's not something worth acting on. It pairs a cheap Polymarket YES, gold touches $4,700 in August contract (4.9 cents) with a Kalshi NO, settles above $4,731.99 on Aug 31 contract (94 cents). After fees the net edge is under a penny per contract, and the live books could only fill 50 contracts total — about 36 cents of profit before considering execution risk. The tiny size is the real story here: this is a rounding-level artifact of thin, low-volume strikes far out in the tails of the distribution, not a genuine mispricing. It's also worth noting the two legs aren't identical bets — Polymarket's contract is a "touch" market (pays out if gold ever trades above $4,700 at any point during August), while Kalshi's is a "settle" market (pays out only based on the price at a specific snapshot, 5pm ET on August 31). The logic linking them still holds, but the structural difference is a reminder that these near-matches are rarely as clean as they look.

Otherwise it's a quiet day: no other cross-platform edges surfaced, and pricing across both venues looks internally consistent with the current rally rather than showing any dislocation.
headline: Gold's August surge to $4,429 leaves prediction markets aligned, with no real arbitrage

sources.title: Gold prices today, Monday, August 10, 2026: Highest opening price since early June - Yahoo Finance
